Compute protein enrichment

Source: R/control_enrichment.R
enrichment.Rd

enrichment() is an analysis function that computes the protein summary statistics for a given tidyproteomics data object.

Usage

enrichment(
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  .pairs = NULL,
  .terms = NULL,
  .method = c("gsea", "wilcoxon", "fishers_exact"),
  .score_type = c("std", "pos", "neg"),
  .log2fc_min = 0,
  .significance_max = 0.05,
  .significance_min = .significance_max,
  .cpu_cores = 1
)

Arguments

data

tidyproteomics data object

...

two sample comparison e.g. experimental/control

.pairs

a list of vectors each containing two named sample groups

.terms

a character string referencing "term(s)" in the annotations table

.method

a character string

.score_type

a character string. From the fgsea manual: "This parameter defines the GSEA score type. Possible options are ("std", "pos", "neg"). By default ("std") the enrichment score is computed as in the original GSEA. The "pos" and "neg" score types are intended to be used for one-tailed tests (i.e. when one is interested only in positive ("pos") or negateive ("neg") enrichment)."

.log2fc_min

used only for Fisher's Exact Test, a numeric defining the minimum log2 foldchange to consider as "enriched"

.significance_max

used only for Fisher's Exact Test, a numeric defining the maximum statistical significance to consider as "enriched"

.significance_min

deprecated alias for .significance_max

.cpu_cores

the number of threads used to speed the calculation

Value

a tibble

Examples

library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(tidyproteomics)

# subset for fast execution
hela_proteins <- hela_proteins %>% subset(description %like% "Ribosome")
#> 
#> ℹ Subsetting data: description %like% Ribosome
#> ✔ Subsetting data: description %like% Ribosome ... done
#> 

# using the default GSEA method
hela_proteins %>%
   expression(knockdown/control) %>%
   enrichment(knockdown/control, .terms = "biological_process") %>%
   export_analysis(knockdown/control, .analysis = "enrichment", .term = "biological_process")
#> ℹ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control
#> ✔ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control [79ms]
#> 
#> ℹ .. enrichment::gsea testing knockdown / control by term biological_process
#> ✔ .. enrichment::gsea testing knockdown / control by term biological_process [6…
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   annotation  p_value adj_p_value enrichment enrichment_normalized log2err  size
#>   <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>      <dbl>                 <dbl>   <dbl> <int>
#> 1 cellular c…   0.396       0.951     -0.429                -1.14   0.194     10
#> 2 metabolic …   0.533       0.951      0.493                 0.975  0.0496     8
#> 3 cell growth   0.592       0.951      0.459                 0.909  0.0448     8
#> 4 cell organ…   0.762       0.951      0.460                 0.816  0.0374     4
#> 5 cell diffe…   0.951       0.951     -0.286                -0.557  0.0749     3

# using a Wilcoxon Rank Sum method
hela_proteins %>%
   expression(knockdown/control) %>%
   enrichment(knockdown/control, .terms = "biological_process", .method = "wilcoxon") %>%
   export_analysis(knockdown/control, .analysis = "enrichment", .term = "biological_process")
#> ℹ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control
#> ✔ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control [64ms]
#> 
#> ℹ .. enrichment::wilcoxon testing knockdown / control by term biological_process
#> ✔ .. enrichment::wilcoxon testing knockdown / control by term biological_proces…
#> 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   annotation                       p_value adj_p_value enrichment  size
#>   <chr>                              <dbl>       <dbl>      <dbl> <int>
#> 1 cellular component movement        0.262       0.736      0.448    10
#> 2 cell organization and biogenesis   0.533       0.736      0.244     4
#> 3 metabolic process                  0.597       0.736      0.526     8
#> 4 cell differentiation               0.659       0.736      0.460     3
#> 5 cell growth                        0.736       0.736      0.526     8

# using the .pairs argument when multiple comparisons are needed
comps <- list(c("control","knockdown"),
            c("knockdown","control"))

hela_proteins %>%
   expression(.pairs = comps) %>%
   enrichment(.pairs = comps, .terms = c("biological_process", "molecular_function"))
#> Expression Analysis - using the supplied 2 sample pairs ...
#> ℹ .. expression::t_test testing control / knockdown
#> ✔ .. expression::t_test testing control / knockdown [66ms]
#> 
#> ℹ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control
#> ✔ .. expression::t_test testing knockdown / control [64ms]
